title: Basil Pesto
subtitle: Italian basil, parmesan, and pine nut sauce
excerpt: A classic Italian sauce of fresh basil, pine nuts, parmesan, and olive oil blitzed together in minutes. It keeps in the fridge for a week and works on pasta, bread, or grilled vegetables.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from Ligurian pesto Genovese tradition. The food processor method is faster than a pestle and mortar and gives a consistent result at home.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in ice cube trays for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Pour into a jar and cover the surface with a thin layer of olive oil. Keeps in the fridge for up to 1 week.

content.text: Pulse rather than blend continuously. Over-blending heats the basil and turns it brown.

items.prepNote: lightly toasted in a dry pan

content.text: Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking often, until lightly golden. Remove immediately and leave to cool.
Put the basil, garlic, and cooled pine nuts in the food processor. Pulse 5 to 6 times until roughly chopped.
Add the parmesan and a pinch of salt. Pulse again 4 to 5 times.
With the processor running, pour in the olive oil in a slow, steady stream. Stop as soon as the oil is incorporated.
Squeeze in the lemon juice. Taste and season with salt. Adjust the consistency with a little more olive oil if needed.
Transfer to a clean jar. Smooth the surface and pour a thin layer of olive oil on top to prevent browning.

items.symptom: Pesto has turned brown rather than bright green.
items.cause: Blended too long and heat from the machine oxidised the basil.
items.fix: Use the pulse function only; never blend continuously.

items.symptom: Pesto is very thick and paste-like.
items.fix: Stir in more oil a tablespoon at a time until the right consistency.

items.cause: Pine nuts were over-toasted or garlic is very strong.
items.fix: Blanch garlic in boiling water for 30 seconds to mellow it.
